gaps: #1 DEFECT, blocked-by P1 (bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/panels/guard.rs, `check()`): the API-path same-origin rule relies on `Sec-Fetch-Site` alone, and Chrome sends NO Sec-Fetch-* to http:// (not a trustworthy origin; verified in the CDP recording: absent on 192.168.77.5, present on 127.0.0.1). So on the LAN origin another origin on the node's host (same site, e.g. a second panel or any local service on another port) can GET the panel's /api/v1/fromradio with the victim's p111 cookie (SameSite=Strict attaches it, Origin/Referer foreign) and gets 200 — the shim pops a frame. The attacker cannot READ it (no CORS, JS fetch rejects) but it destroys the viewer's frames. Evidence: lan/probe.same-site-get (Chrome) + 3 curl checks (foreign Origin+Referer, nothing-dequeued, Referer-only ). Loopback origins are fine (localhost/probe.same-site-get -> 403 same-site). Cross-site on the LAN is safe (cookie withheld -> 401). §20 G3's 'cross-site GET from a second netns origin dequeues nothing' therefore passes; the same-site variant (guard.rs' own doc, P1 review m1) does not. Fix verified in a scratch copy: refuse a foreign Origin/Referer on API paths when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent (patch in notes).

#2 RESIDUAL, spec decision (not a failure; printed as `note: RESIDUAL`): even after #1, a same-site no-cors GET with referrerPolicy no-referrer carries no Origin, no Referer, no Sec-Fetch-* and is byte-identical to the panel's own same-origin GET (the panel sets Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; the dashboard does too, so a frame navigated from the dashboard is the same case: lan/probe.stealth-get, lan/probe.dashboard-frame-get). Over plain HTTP on a LAN IP nothing server-side separates them; closing it needs a per-origin proof the unmodified Meshtastic client cannot send (or serving panels from a trustworthy origin). Owner: spec/lead (§13 'Guards' wording promises more than http://<LAN IP> can deliver).

#3 NOT ASSERTED, external gate: the real Meshtastic web client bundle is not on this box (find / found none). The run is against the placeholder (cdp/placeholder-bundle: index.html + app.js calling PUT /api/v1/toradio and GET /api/v1/fromradio?all=true, own-origin only). So unverified for the real bundle: its actual off-origin hosts (tiles.openfreemap.org, api.meshtastic.org — declared optional hosts would only print a note), inline scripts/handlers, service workers, the connect-dialog prefill (the lint's prefill check is the placeholder's own location.host; with PANEL_LINT_BUNDLE the driver reports any input holding the panel authority as ok/note). The `--bundle-kind real` path was exercised only with the placeholder directory passed as PANEL_LINT_BUNDLE (green), never with a real build.

#4 NOT ASSERTED, external gate: meshmud is a Python stub speaking the 0x94 0xC3 framing with JSON payloads standing in for protobufs (one frame per node, each < 512 B). Real meshmud behaviour (serial open, config fan-out to a second client, per-session downlinks against a real board) is the spec's hardware external gate.

#5 FINDING outside my files (owner V1/lead): interface/verify/smoke.sh `jb()` is `jq -e … "$W/body"`, and `jq -e` exits 0 on EMPTY input, so every `jb`/`t` check that is meant to match JSON passes vacuously on an empty body (I hit it: 'frame 2 = node list' passed while the body was empty; mine now guards with `[ -s body ]`). I did not audit which smoke checks are affected.

#6 NOTE for later (not a gap today): cookies are port-blind, so every request to the panel origin carries the dashboard's HttpOnly s111 cookie (17/17 in the LAN run) and the dashboard receives p111_*; the static+shim server ignores it, the panel JS cannot read it. A future generic proxy (P7) must strip s111/p111_* as §13 already says (printed as `note: lan/cookie.port-blind`).
deviations: Default run is RED by design while gap #1 stands (the task's check was 'green'). `PANEL_LINT_KNOWN_GAPS=1` turns only the 'GAP (blocked-by …)' checks into notes and gives GREEN; with the guard.rs patch the default run is GREEN with no switch. I kept strict as the default so the gate cannot go green while the defect exists.

Declared `[offline] optional_hosts` (tiles.openfreemap.org, api.meshtastic.org) are allowed with a `note` (spec §13), not failed; any other host the panel touches is FAIL. The brief's 'no request leaves the panel origin' is enforced for every undeclared host (proved by the canary).

'Cross-origin fetch of /fromradio from the dashboard origin refused (403)': a fetch from the dashboard page never reaches the panel — the dashboard's CSP `connect-src 'self'` blocks it (asserted, with the CSP violation as evidence), so no 403 exists to observe. The 403 is asserted for (a) a frame inside the dashboard navigating to the API and (b) fetches from another origin on the host (loopback scenario: 403 with Sec-Fetch-Site same-site/cross-site). On the LAN origin (a) and the same-site fetch are the gap #1/#2 cases; the cross-site fetch there answers 401 (cookie withheld), accepted as 'refused, nothing dequeued'.

Bundle path follows the manifest (`current/panels/meshtastic-web`), not `current/panels/meshtastic/` as the brief wrote. The placeholder is committed under cdp/placeholder-bundle and copied into the scratch root rather than written at runtime.

Added beyond the brief: a `localhost` scenario (308 -> 127.0.0.1, implicit session), a hostile canary bundle the lint must flag, probes from a same-site and a cross-site origin, Reload re-mint + spent-ticket replay, a curl matrix (ticket swap, Set-Cookie bytes, guards, SPA fallback, shim echo round trip, dequeue-nothing, drive-by POST/PUT, upgrade, byte-for-byte bundle serving, only-expected-LAN-listeners), a rule self-test (74 checks), cdp/README.md. No SSE tape was added (none needed), so the tapes README is untouched.
Also added a 4-step pre-run: `selftest.mjs` runs before the daemon so a rule that cannot fail is caught first.
